project.title: SSC CSD R&D
project.role: AWS Cloud Infrastructure as Code DevOps Engineer & Architect

role_overview.summary: Within Shared Services Canada (SSC), the Cloud Services Directorate (CSD) Research and Development (R&D) group carried a mandate to create reusable, government-grade Infrastructure as Code for adoption across SSC and its federal partner departments. Christian served as AWS Cloud Infrastructure as Code DevOps Engineer and Architect on this engagement, leading the design and delivery of the CSD Landing Zone, a multi-account AWS foundation built first on AWS Landing Zone and later on the AWS Secure Environment Accelerator (ASEA). He also built an organization-shared AWS Service Catalog offering blueprint and operational products, and federated AWS access with Azure Active Directory through AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) Identity Center. In addition, Christian implemented the information technology (IT) security program that achieved interim Authority to Operate (iATO) in September 2020, and the CSD Landing Zone became SSC's standard AWS landing zone.

challenge.summary: Across Shared Services Canada (SSC), teams operated AWS workloads in stand-alone or loosely coupled accounts with no shared standard for security, governance, or financial accountability. The Cloud Services Directorate (CSD) needed a reusable cloud platform that could meet Information Technology Security Guidance (ITSG-22, ITSG-33, and ITSG-38) and Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat (TBS) cloud guardrails and gain an Authority to Operate (ATO), despite having no precedent for authorising cloud systems.

deliverables: Multi-Account Build of the Cloud Services Directorate (CSD) Landing Zone
AWS IAM Identity Center Federation with Azure Active Directory
Interim Authority to Operate Security Program for the Cloud Services Directorate (CSD) Landing Zone

outcomes: Interim Authority to Operate (iATO) was granted for the Cloud Services Directorate (CSD) Landing Zone in September 2020
The CSD Landing Zone became Shared Services Canada's (SSC) standard AWS landing zone, with 3 early adopter workload clients onboarded
